upstream.snapshot: git archive --format=tar --prefix=FreeCAD-<commit>/ <commit> -- <the five replay FILES> | gzip -n
upstream.snapshotScope: The five importer files only, taken from the pinned Git commit; the archive is scratch-only.

candidate.state: Twenty pre-existing downstream patches applied as uncommitted changes to five files in a disposable sparse checkout; no FreeCAD commit, branch push, or pull request was made.
candidate.diff: 1964 insertions and 19 deletions across five files; review and split the combined candidate into coherent contributions before submission.
candidate.lineEndings: The source dxf.h has CRLF throughout; the replay restores CRLF after applying the historical normalized patches. Git diff is checked with core.whitespace=cr-at-eol.

checks: The 20 existing patches apply in order to the pinned current source. The replay validates the source archive digest, applies in temporary storage, checks the five-file inventory, and matches all prepared candidate file hashes.
A dirty-checkout reapplication and a corrupted source archive both refused while leaving all five prepared file hashes unchanged.

The new CTest libdxfrw_freecad_patch_replay passes three synthetic controls: preserve pure CRLF and LF, refuse mixed source endings before publication, and retain historical normalization for earlier baselines. The CTest uses git apply and generated text only.
The FreeCAD checkout passes a CRLF-aware git diff --check, and its patched Python test file compiles syntactically. No native build or runtime test was run on this source revision.
limits: Patch application and syntax are not a FreeCAD build, runtime, native GUI, interoperability, or source-wire qualification. The pinned source and candidate must be built and exercised before reuse of platform claims.
Existing patches still refuse or leave unqualified nonplanar faces, hidden edges, smoothing and other graph and visual profiles; they do not establish general FreeCAD mesh support.
FreeCAD AGENTS.md and AI_POLICY.md reserve repository communication and contributor attestations for the human contributor. No submission or human review is claimed.
